days.title: Glaciers and Peaks of Alpe Veglia
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Ghiacciaio del Leone
stops.detail: The glacial origin of the basins is evidenced by the persistence of some residues of ancient glaciers, such as the Leone Glacier and the Aurona Glacier from Alpe Veglia or the Rossa Glacier from the Alpe Devero side.

stops.name: Monte Leone
stops.detail: To the north, Alpe Veglia is surrounded by Mount Helsenhorn (3,272 m a.s.l.), Mount Mottiscia (3,156 m a.s.l.), Mount Rebbio (3,192 m a.s.l.), Punta d'Aurona (2,984 m a.s.l.), Punta di Terrarossa (3,246 m a.s.l.), and Mount Leone (3,553 m a.s.l.).

stops.name: Lago delle Streghe
stops.detail: There is a ferruginous water spring and the Witches' Lake.

stops.name: Pizzo Cervandone
stops.detail: Alpe Devero is also a basin of glacial origin and is surrounded to the north by Punta d'Arbola (3,235 m a.s.l.), Albrunhorn (2,840 m a.s.l., also known as Mount Figascian), Punta di Valdeserta (2,939 m a.s.l.), Punta della Rossa (2,888 m a.s.l.), Punta Marani (3,108 m a.s.l.), Pizzo Cervandone (3,155 m a.s.l.), and Pizzo Cornera (3,083 m a.s.l.).

stops.name: Monte Cazzola
stops.detail: In winter, ski lifts are available on Mount Cazzola as well as cross-country ski trails and various walks (to be chosen based on one's experience level) practicable with ski mountaineering and snowshoes.
